title: Sunday worship
hookLine: gathering with others around word and table
tomorrow: God rested on the seventh day. so which day do Christians rest?

cards: Somebody always nods off in the back row. Acts keeps a story about one who nodded off in a window. Late at night in Troas, an upstairs room is bright with lamps, and Paul, leaving in the morning, talks until midnight.

A young man named Eutychus sinks into a deep sleep and falls from the third loft. Acts says they took him up dead. Paul runs down, wraps his arms around him, and says: “Trouble not yourselves; for his life is in him.”
A book with a whole world to cover stops for this. Why?

teach.b: Look at what happens next, because that's the clue. Nobody goes home. Paul goes back upstairs, breaks bread, eats, and talks with them till daybreak.
A fall from the third loft didn't end the meeting. So what were they all doing up there?

teach.h: THE FIRST DAY, TO BREAK BREAD.
teach.b: Acts says it in the King James Bible: “upon the first day of the week, when the disciples came together to break bread.” The gathering was the point.
Earlier in Acts, the first believers had the same pattern: “they continued stedfastly in the apostles' doctrine and fellowship, and in breaking of bread, and in prayers.”
Word and table, together. Why the first day? It's the day Luke's Gospel says the women came to the tomb and found it empty, and Christians came to call it the Lord's day.
Churches keep that gathering in different ways. Some share communion every Sunday; others share it less often and center the morning on scripture and preaching. Some gather on Saturday instead.
The letter to the Hebrews puts the instinct plainly: “Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together.”
That's the answer to the puzzle. Luke keeps the boy in the window because the story is about a room nobody wanted to leave.

how: On Sunday morning, churches gather for scripture, prayer, singing and preaching; some share communion every Sunday and others less often, and some churches gather on Saturday instead.

games.q: your cousin moved to a new city months ago. she watches a sermon alone on Sunday and says that covers it. what does the night in Troas nudge her toward?
o: finding people to gather with, around word and table.
keeping the sermon; the teaching is the whole point.
waiting until she finds the perfect church first.
games.why: in Acts the point was coming together: word and table, fellowship and prayers. Hebrews says not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together.

practice: Make a small plan for this week. Name the gathering you'd want to be part of, name the one thing most likely to keep you away, and then decide what you'll do when that thing shows up: if this happens, then I'll do that.
Keep it small enough to be true: one gathering, one obstacle, one answer.

wordCard.voice: Sunday worship. People coming together on the first day of the week, around word and table, and staying even after the fall.

orig.note: the New Testament's Greek word usually translated church: an assembly.

carryVoice: Carry this: gather, the way Troas did, when even a fall from a window sent nobody home. Day 1696, kept.
